title: CheckLink: additions required by the approved spec that provider-rules.json does not cover
why: provider-rules.json is the verified table of tracking parameters and redirect wrappers. The approved spec (LabsIdeas/CheckLink - spec 2026-10-10.md) also asks for a protected-name guard, general-purpose short-link and dynamic-QR services (warning 6), the ;jsessionid= path segment, the leave-untouched list and recipient tokens kept on unsubscribe pages. Those live here so the verified table stays as delivered. The review of 10 October 2026 added three more sections: suffix_deny (look-alike suffixes the provider patterns must not accept; removed on 11 October 2026 in version 1.6.1, when stage 2 shipped the Public Suffix List, which now decides them), additions (wrappers and parameters the big providers use that the table lacks) and corrections (targeted fixes to six table entries, each with its reason). Marcos's Instagram test of the same day added canonical (pages fully addressed by their path, where a parameter on no list is shown as Unrecognised and removed by default). tools/build-rules.mjs merges everything into src/rules.js. Decision IG-1 of 11 October 2026 (stage 4b): every instagram.com rule also applies to instagr.am, by extension, not checked online: the host rules as an addition and the canonical-page rule by its hosts.

protected_names.source: Spec section 2, 'Never removed on every site'. tools/build-rules.mjs refuses a global rule that could remove one of these on every site.
protected_names.allowed_global_exceptions: A global rule on a protected name is accepted only when its default is keep, or when a requires_any condition ties it to a vendor's own companion parameter (for example AppsFlyer c only next to af_xp).

short_links.source: Spec section 3, warning 6 names bit.ly, t.co and qrco.de. t.co and the platform shorteners (lnkd.in, amzn.to, pin.it and others) are already redirects in provider-rules.json; this list adds general-purpose services. A host matches itself and its subdomains. Checked online on 10 October 2026 (curl, no cookies, a Firefox user agent, real codes found in public code): every service still answers and redirects as assumed. t.ly puts every automated request behind a Cloudflare challenge, so it was checked in a real browser instead on 11 October 2026 (Marcos): https://t.ly/_Vu9 goes straight to https://github.com/mmaaz60/EdgeNeXt, with nothing added to the address. Noted: v.gd and sometimes is.gd show a preview page naming the destination before going on; goo.gl links with no activity in late 2024 were switched off by Google, while active ones and Google-app links still redirect; QR Code Generator also serves its codes from q-r.to and l.ead.me.

path_rules.source: Spec section 2, order of work, step 1: ';jsessionid=' is removed with a warning. Search engines (10 October 2026): Yahoo's ;_ylt= click tracking and the session segments Baidu writes before /s on m.baidu.com, each limited to its own hosts. Batch 3 review (10 October 2026): the Yahoo rule is anchored to a result path (finding P7) and the Baidu rule takes every name=value segment before /s (finding P6).

rules.name: ;_ylt= (path segment)

rules.basis: Verified: search-engine research of 10 October 2026 (mainstream.verified.json, Yahoo Search): observed on every Yahoo link that day; SearXNG and Yahoo's own links. Batch 3 review finding P7 (10 October 2026): anchored to the end of a result path such as /search, so it never edits the middle of the r.search.yahoo.com click redirect, which is unwrapped instead.

rules.name: /ssid=, /from=, /baiduid= (path segments)
rules.reveals: A session ID, Baidu's visitor ID from its cookie (baiduid), your screen size and a partner code, written into the address before /s.
rules.basis: Verified: search-engine research of 10 October 2026 (asia.verified.json, Baidu): Baidu's own mobile link builder (edpx-zhixin function.wiseMakeSearchUrl.php) writes these segments before /s. Batch 3 review finding P6 (10 October 2026): every name=value segment before the last part of the path goes, uid and baiduid (the BAIDUID cookie, Baidu's own visitor ID) included, so the Baidu result-page rule then applies to /s.

canonical.source: Marcos's test of 10 October 2026: an Instagram post link carried mdxt=, a parameter no list names (its value is base64 of an identifier), so the deny-list kept it. A list of known trackers always lags behind the platforms. On the pages below the address is the path alone: the post, video or product is named by the ID in the path, and the page opens the same without any query or key=value fragment. On these pages, and only there, a parameter that no verified rule names, that the rule's keep list does not name and that no functional_keep entry keeps is shown as Unrecognised and ticked by default; it can be unticked like any other part, and the clean link then keeps it byte for byte. A protected short name (protected_names) is shown as Unrecognised too, but unticked (reveals_ask), because those names often choose what a page shows (canonical review finding C5, 10 October 2026). Language choices (hl, lang, language) and the Spotify collaborator invite (pt) are on the keep lists (findings C1 and C3). Verified trackers keep their own labels. Never applied to a link left untouched (signed, sign-in or reset values, Proofpoint) or to any other path of these sites. Hosts are matched exactly: a name.* entry stands for that name under the suffix pattern, with nothing in front of it. Paths are regular expressions anchored at both ends, matched against the path with the parts removed by default cut out (Amazon /ref=). tools/build-rules.mjs refuses an unanchored path, a host entry that is not one exact name, and a keep name that a rule for the same hosts removes. Basis: structural, from the URL formats the verified table already records (functional_keep instagram-threads, x, tiktok, youtube, spotify, amazon-product); checked against real links on 10 October 2026 (online-verification report): /<user>/p/<code>/?img_index=, /@<user>/post/<code>, /i/web/status/<id>, /@<user>/photo/<id>, /intl-xx/ Spotify items with highlight= and pt=, Amazon /-/<lang>/.../dp/<ASIN> and aod=1, and LinkedIn ugcPost posts with commentUrn and replyUrn all clean as the rules intend. Search-engine result pages and LinkedIn posts joined on 10 October 2026 (Marcos's tests M4, M9, M10 and M11, spec decisions 12 to 14): their keep and remove lists come from the verified research of that day (one file per group of engines, each parameter with its sources), so each of those rules cites a Verified basis. A keep entry may hold only under a condition (when: paths, or clauses on the other parameters, such as DuckDuckGo's ia only when it chooses a tab other than the web results); when the condition fails, otherwise gives the label it is removed under. The remove list names parameters verified to do nothing on those pages: each is removed by default with its own label, even a protected short name (DuckDuckGo t, Brave source). A rule may require (requires) or exclude (unless) parameters before it applies, which lets a home page with ?q= count as a result page and lets SearXNG, which runs on any host, be recognised by its own parameters. On Baidu and Naver an empty value is dropped (drop_empty), as the research allows. Batch 3 review (10 October 2026): SearXNG is recognised on any host only by values SearXNG itself writes (finding P1), LinkedIn comment links keep the comment (P2), Google Lens and Bing visual-search pages are left to the verified rules (P3, L5), Bing keeps safesearch as spec decision 12 says (P10), item selectors inside Google and Yandex result pages are kept (L1, L3), and remove entries may say perClick true or false so the badge follows what the value is rather than its shape (interface review finding 7). Spec decisions of 10 October 2026: Bing's search-box and session values are host rules now, so they go on every bing.com path and not only on these pages (decision 20, finding L4); DuckDuckGo iai, the item open in the side panel, is removed as the research says, reversing finding L2 (decision 22); TikTok t on a video or photo page is removed by default with its own label (decision 23).

rules.basis: Structural: a LinkedIn post is addressed by /posts/<slug>-<activity id>-<code>/ or /feed/update/urn:li:activity:<id>/ (the verified table's linkedin-paths entry). The urn:li:share and urn:li:ugcPost forms are LinkedIn's own post IDs: LinkedIn's Posts API documentation (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/marketing/community-management/shares/posts-api, read 10 October 2026) names both as post IDs and gives https://www.linkedin.com/feed/update/urn:li:ugcPost:<id>/ as the address of a published post. Marcos's test M4 of 10 October 2026: highlightedUpdateUrn, highlightedUpdateType and origin point to a reshare and the post opens without them. Two-letter country hosts (no.linkedin.com) serve the same pages. Profiles, jobs and every other path are not covered. Sign-in values (otpToken stays an 'ask' part through its verified rule) are never touched by this rule. Batch 3 review finding P2 (10 October 2026): commentUrn and dashCommentUrn (with replyUrn and dashReplyUrn for a reply) are what LinkedIn's 'Copy link to comment' writes; they open that comment, so they stay.

SearXNG runs on any host, so the rule applies only on /search or the instance root (optionally under a path prefix) with q and values only SearXNG writes together: a category switch named after one of its own categories (category_general, category_images and the other tabs), theme=simple with safesearch 0, 1 or 2, pageno with language and safesearch, categories naming only SearXNG's own categories with language or safesearch, engine_data-..., timeout_limit, or one of its preference names. Batch 3 review finding P1 (10 October 2026): pageno, time_range, engines or a category_ prefix on their own are not enough, because ordinary sites use them too (a shop's category_id, a list paged with pageno), and the rule would then strip those sites' own parameters. Stage 4b review (12 October 2026, findings S3 and SC-5): the rule no longer names any instance by its host, so no private instance's names ship with the website or the app; an instance's own pages are recognised by the values SearXNG writes, as on any other host.

untouched.source: Spec section 2, 'Some links are left untouched'. Checked on the final address, after offline unwrapping, so a wrapper's own sig or token never blocks unwrapping. A signed entry needs every name in all and, when it has any, at least one of those too: an Azure SAS link always carries sv (signed version) or se (expiry) next to sig, while Google Books and others use a lone sig that signs nothing (review finding F18). auth_params are looked for in the query, in key=value fragments and in the query part of a route fragment (#/callback?code=...), review finding F19.

recipient_tokens.source: Spec section 2, 'Kept where they are needed'. provider-rules.json keeps mkt_tok on such pages but strips the other three everywhere; the spec keeps all four here. page_words are matched against the words of the path segments and of the query parameter NAMES, never against values (review finding F5: utm_campaign=optout_reminder on a blog page is not an opt-out page). A segment or name counts when its first or last word is one of them (manage-preferences, UnsubscribePage.html, mkt_unsubscribe); opt-out and opt_out count as optout.
